subject.title: feat(skills): add option to disable ~/.agents/skills scanning for Claude Code coexistence

question: Should OpenClaw add a public opt-out for the built-in personal `~/.agents/skills` source, and if so should the config be a general typed source-disable list or a narrower personal-source toggle?
rationale: The source-level problem is clear, but repository policy sets a high bar for new config surface and the choice affects a documented built-in skill source, watcher behavior, status output, docs, and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Add a typed source-disable list
options.body: Expose a narrow `skills.load` setting for named built-in sources and make discovery, watchers, status, docs, and tests honor it while preserving current defaults when unset.

options.title: Add only a personal-source toggle
options.body: Solve this issue with a smaller `~/.agents/skills` opt-out, but accept a less extensible contract if other built-in roots later need similar handling.

options.title: Keep current source model
options.body: Decline the source opt-out and steer users to skill allowlists, prompt budgets, or per-skill disables, leaving scanning and precedence unchanged.

recommendation.title: Add a typed source-disable list
recommendation.body: Expose a narrow `skills.load` setting for named built-in sources and make discovery, watchers, status, docs, and tests honor it while preserving current defaults when unset.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main blame and adjacent issue handling place this account closest to the present skills loader, watcher, config, and docs surfaces.
